t: The vertices of a triangle are (pq,1/pq), (qr,1/qr) and (rp,1/rp) where p,q,r are the roots of the equation y³−3y²+6y+1=0. The coordinates of its centroid are:
s:
Given the cubic equation y³−3y²+6y+1=0 with roots p,q,r.
From the properties of roots of a cubic equation:
Sum of roots: p+q+r=−(−3)/1=3
Sum of product of roots taken two at a time: pq+qr+rp=6/1=6
Product of roots: pqr=−1/1=−1
The vertices of the triangle are (pq,1/pq), (qr,1/qr) and (rp,1/rp).
The x-coordinate of the centroid is given by:
x_c=(pq+qr+rp)/3=6/3=2
The y-coordinate of the centroid is given by:
y_c=(1/pq+1/qr+1/rp)/3=((r+p+q)/pqr)/3=(p+q+r)/3pqr
Substituting the values of the sum and product of roots:
y_c=3/(3(−1))=3/(−3)=−1
Therefore, the coordinates of the centroid are (2,−1).
